transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-16
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Liam Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (Redwood CSM); Aisha Kapoor, Jon Bramwell, Sara Li, Marco (Crestline)

Summary (auto): Quick recap of pilot throughput, discussed tuning knobs for continuous batching, queueing thresholds, and how to validate sustained throughput without cost blowout.

[00:00] Liam: hey everyone thanks for joining on a tuesday, um we wanted to run through the last 48 hours of the pilot and then pick a small set of experiments to run this week.
[00:12] Aisha: yeah thanks liam, we saw the spike yesterday around 03:00 UTC — throughput dropped then latency jumped, so curious if that was batching behavior or a concurrency throttle.
[00:24] Sofia: quick note, we saw two things: the batcher window tightened under low qps and some requests hit the concurrency cap which pushed them into queue and increased tail.
[00:36] Jon: when you say "batcher window tightened" do you mean the continuous batcher auto-shrank? I thought it would keep grouping until X ms.
[00:44] Sofia: right so continuous batching has a soft target, it will aggregate until either max_wait_ms or batch_size then dispatch. under spiky arrival patterns it can oscillate — we logged the batch size distribution in the heatmap. link: https://redwood.internal/drive/crestline/heatmap-feb16 (note: internal link).
[01:02] Sara: the other concern from our side is cost: if we bump concurrency to hit the p95 target, our monthly GPU hours increase a lot. what's the recommended sweet spot?
[01:12] Liam: good question. typical tradeoff: higher concurrency lowers token latency per-request but increases active GPU time. for crestline's workload (short prompts, high qps), we recommend concurrency in the 24-48 range with prefix caching to reduce compute.
[01:27] Marco: prefix caching — you mean the KV cache? we did a quick warmup but not a full prewarm. some of the cold misses are expensive.
[01:36] Sofia: yes, kay-vee cache, the kv cache. if you prewarm cold keys for the top 10k prefixes you get a big p95 improvement. we can share a script — small snippet in the runbook.
[01:48] Aisha: can we see the log lines that show the cache hit ratio? yesterday it was around 68% and we expected 85%.
[01:55] Daniel: we pulled the metrics — the hit ratio drop correlates with the morning burst when a new model variant got routed in. routing fallback caused some cold-booting.
[02:06] Jon: wait, routing fallback — are we talking about the smart routing policy where requests move to cheaper variant on overload?
[02:12] Liam: yes, we had a brief period where the primary variant hit resource pressure and the router sent traffic to a lower-heap quantized variant. that variant has slightly different KV layout and that explains misses.
[02:23] Sara: that's helpful. how do we prevent that in pilot? we need stability for production-looking numbers.
[02:30] Sofia: two knobs: 1) pin the variant for the pilot, disable automatic fallback; 2) increase reserved pool briefly during expected bursts (burst capacity). for the first week we usually pin and run a controlled burst.
[02:44] Aisha: ok pinning sounds safe. about the queue — can you explain the backpressure behavior? sometimes requests time out waiting in queue.
[02:53] Sofia: the queue has a soft ttl and we surface backpressure metrics. if inflight+queued > max_inflight_threshold, the router will begin shedding lowest-priority requests. we can tune ttl and priority rules.
[03:06] Jon: the timeouts we saw were ~12s — our client defaults to 10s which explains the client-side failures.
[03:12] Daniel: quick reminder: SDK defaults differ from our platform defaults, we should sync on those. action item: Sofia to send the recommended SDK timeouts.
[03:20] Liam: noted. ok let's look at the numbers from 14th-15th (screen share). [screen share noise]
[03:34] Sofia: 48-hour summary: sustained avg qps 1.9k, 95th latency ~410ms when cache warm, p95 jumped to 1.1s during the 03:00 UTC burst, avg batch size 6, peak batch size 22.
[03:48] Aisha: the jump to 1.1s correlates with new model rollout — is that in our control?
[03:53] Sofia: you can pin model versions at the route level, that prevents auto-rollout for the pilot.
[03:58] Marco: we noticed also CPU saturation on the orchestration host during burst; could that be a factor?
[04:04] Sofia: possible — if the host can't feed data to GPU fast enough you get queuing. we saw small IO stutters in the agent logs around that time. Jon, can you check host metrics?
[04:12] Jon: yes will do.
[04:14] Sara: security question — for SOC2 we need audit logs showing model ID and request metadata retained for 90 days. does Redwood keep those for pilots?
[04:24] Liam: we retain a configurable audit trail; for Private/Dedicated we can meet 90 days. hosted pilots default to 30 days but we can enable extended retention for enterprise pilots — need an agreed contract addendum.
[04:37] Aisha: ok please put that in writing.
[04:40] Daniel: noted, liam will follow up with contract addendum note.
[04:45] Sofia: back to experiments: proposal for this week — run two tests: 1) Controlled 2-hour burst (concurrency 48, pinned variant, kv prewarm), 2) Adaptive batching enabled for 6 hrs to measure latency improvement vs cost.
[04:59] Aisha: number 1 we agree; number 2 we worry about oscillation causing tail spikes. can you bound risk?
[05:05] Sofia: yes we can set conservative adaptive thresholds and watch batch size histogram in real time. if p95 worsens we'll revert.
[05:12] Jon: planning note: we'll run the burst test in our staging env first to validate host IO and then the pilot.
[05:18] Liam: good. next, metrics — we want to baseline two things: cost per 1k requests and p95 latency under sustained load. if those look good we'll scale up to 3k qps next week.
[05:30] Sara: what's the expected cost delta if we go from concurrency 24 -> 48?
[05:33] Liam: rough ballpark is +30-40% GPU-hour; but per-request cost goes down because you reduce wasted idle time. we'll provide a model for this.
[05:43] Aisha: can we also capture the exact SDK timeouts recommended and an example prewarm script?
[05:48] Sofia: yes will add both to runbook — example prewarm CLI and best-practice SDK timeouts.
[05:54] Jon: small nit: can Redwood surface the queue depth in the API response or at least a header so our instrumentation can flag imminent queueing?
[06:02] Sofia: not currently in the header but we can push a header that indicates queue position; we need product ok but for a pilot we can enable an experiment flag.
[06:12] Aisha: that'd be very helpful.
[06:15] Liam: let's capture action items — Sofia to post runbook, Aisha to share traffic sample, Jon to run host IO test, Liam to send pilot pricing and contract note for retention. we'll reconvene after the 2-hour burst test to review logs.
[06:30] Aisha: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:33] Sara: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps and internal links sometimes mis-labeled, some product names transcribed phonetically ("kay-vee cache").
